title: Kotlin Coroutines vs. Flow: Enforcing Cardinality in API Signatures
metricImpact: -32% boilerplate allocations · zero leaked subscriptions in ViewModel layer
context: Engineers were wrapping every repository call in `Flow<Result<T>>`, including one-shot POST mutations and single-row lookups. Stack traces blurred across operator chains, and callers had to guess whether a function emitted once and completed or stayed hot indefinitely.

options.name: Flow<T> for all async boundaries
options.summary: Uniform reactive API, but forces cold-stream allocation, `first()` ceremony on one-shot calls, and ambiguous completion semantics.

options.name: suspend fun everywhere + manual callbacks
options.summary: Simple for RPCs, but cannot compose database invalidation, WebSocket frames, or multi-source state conflation cleanly.

options.name: Strict cardinality split: suspend for 1, Flow for N
options.summary: One-shot operations are `suspend fun`; continuous observation (Room tables, WebSockets, sensor streams) returns `Flow<T>`.

decision: Enforce a strict lint and review rule: if an operation produces at most one value, its signature is `suspend fun` returning a typed result (`Result<T>` or sealed domain error). `Flow<T>` is reserved exclusively for multi-emission streams and converted to `StateFlow` at the ViewModel boundary via `stateIn(viewModelScope, SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5_000), initial)`.
why: The function signature encodes temporal behavior without reading the implementation.
`WhileSubscribed(5_000)` keeps upstream Room/WebSocket collectors alive across configuration changes while tearing them down 5 seconds after the UI goes to background.
Structured concurrency (`coroutineScope` + `SupervisorJob`) gives deterministic cancellation and readable stack traces for transactional writes.

title: Jetpack Compose Recomposition Control vs. Legacy View System at Scale
metricImpact: Scroll jank cut from 18.2% → 4.9% on 3GB Android 11 reference device
context: During a 90-screen fintech migration, a high-frequency transaction feed regressed from 58fps in `RecyclerView` to 44fps in Compose. Layout Inspector revealed 60+ unnecessary row recompositions per fling because domain models held `java.time.Instant` and `kotlin.collections.List`.

options.name: Keep complex feeds in RecyclerView / AndroidView
options.summary: Predictable recycling performance, but splits theming, accessibility semantics, and state hosting across two UI toolkits.

options.name: Patch call sites with remember() and derivedStateOf()
options.summary: Suppresses individual symptoms but leaves unstable parameter types in the Compose compiler report.

options.name: Compiler-verified stability + lambda state reads + Baseline Profiles
options.summary: Enforce `@Immutable` UI models, `ImmutableList<T>`, method-reference callbacks, and AOT Baseline Profiles.

decision: Stay 100% Jetpack Compose, enable `-P plugin:androidx.compose.compiler.plugins.kotlin:reportsDestination` in CI, replace `List<T>` in UI state with `kotlinx.collections.immutable.ImmutableList<T>`, wrap external types in `@Immutable` value classes, and ship a Macrobenchmark-generated Baseline Profile with every release.
why: Fixing stability at the type declaration lets the Compose slot table skip entire subtrees in O(1) equality checks.
Deferring scroll-dependent reads into lambda modifiers (`Modifier.offset { ... }`, `Modifier.drawBehind { ... }`) skips composition and layout phases entirely, running only in draw.
Baseline Profiles pre-compile hot Compose paths to native machine code at install time, eliminating JIT warmup jank on first launch.

title: MVVM vs. MVI for State Management in Complex Multi-Step Screens
metricImpact: Zero impossible-state UI bugs in payment & sync flows over 12 months
context: Screens with simple read-only lists worked well with classic MVVM, but complex flows (biometric payment confirmation, offline conflict resolution, live transit filtering) accumulated 7–10 independent `MutableStateFlow` fields in a single ViewModel, causing race conditions between loading spinners and error banners.

options.name: Pure MVVM with multiple StateFlows per screen
options.summary: Low ceremony on simple screens, but permits exponential combinations of boolean flags (`isLoading && hasError && isSuccess`).

options.name: Heavyweight Redux/MVI framework across every screen
options.summary: Total determinism, but forces boilerplate reducers and action classes onto trivial settings and static detail screens.

options.name: Pragmatic MVI: single sealed UiState + unidirectional Intent channel
options.summary: One `StateFlow<UiState>`, one `onIntent(UiIntent)` entry point, and a `Channel<UiEffect>` for one-off navigation/biometric prompts.

decision: Standardize on a lightweight, zero-dependency MVI contract for interactive screens: a single immutable `UiState` (using sealed interfaces for mutually exclusive screen phases), a pure reducer transition for state mutations, and a `Channel<UiEffect>(Channel.BUFFERED)` consumed with `repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED)` for one-shot side effects.
why: A single `StateFlow<UiState>` guarantees atomic renders — Compose never observes half-updated screen state.
Testing becomes deterministic: given initial state `S` and intent `I`, assert the exact sequence of emitted states with `Turbine` in <15ms on the JVM.
Separating `UiEffect` via a buffered `Channel` prevents duplicate biometric dialogs or navigation events on screen rotation.

title: Offline-First Sync (WorkManager + Room Outbox) vs. Direct Real-Time Push
metricImpact: 99.4% mutation delivery across 2G/3G dead zones · -67% stale-state bugs
context: Both field operations and urban transit apps face intermittent connectivity, captive portals, and OS background execution limits. Direct REST/WebSocket writes from the UI layer failed silently when the app was backgrounded mid-request or when connections dropped inside tunnels.

options.name: Optimistic UI + direct network writes in ViewModel
options.summary: Fastest initial implementation, but process death or Doze mode drops in-flight mutations permanently.

options.name: Persistent Foreground Service with live socket
options.summary: Immediate push delivery, but triggers user-dismissible notifications on Android 13+ and drains battery.

options.name: Room Single Source of Truth + Durable Outbox + WorkManager
options.summary: All writes commit locally to an outbox transaction first; WorkManager drains mutations; WebSockets/FCM only trigger delta pulls into Room.

decision: The UI never reads from the network and never awaits a remote write. Mutations write atomically to a local `Room` entity + `outbox_commands` table with a client UUID, then enqueue a unique `WorkManager` job (`ExistingWorkPolicy.APPEND_OR_REPLACE`) with network constraints and exponential backoff. Real-time WebSockets/FCM act purely as invalidation or delta-ingest signals into Room.
why: Survives process death, device reboot, and airplane mode by construction — the user's work is durable the millisecond the local SQLite transaction commits.
Client-generated UUID idempotency keys allow WorkManager to retry safely without duplicating financial transfers or field reports.
Exposing `SyncStatus` (`SYNCED`, `PENDING`, `CONFLICT`) as a column on the Room entity lets the UI render honest freshness indicators without network coupling.
